details.title: Describe Your Neighborhood
details.description: Learn to describe your neighborhood using 'there is/are' and prepositions of place. Practice using descriptive adjectives.
details.theorySummary: rule: To list what your neighborhood has, use 'There is' for singular items (e.g., 'There is a park.') and 'There are' for plural items (e.g., 'There are many shops.'). | example: Correct: 'My house is next to a supermarket.' or 'There is a school on the main street.' (Uses 'next to', 'on' to show position). Incorrect: 'My house supermarket.' (Missing preposition). Prepositions like 'in', 'on', 'near', 'next to', 'opposite' are essential. | tip: Use adjectives to describe the general feeling or…
sampleStems: My neighborhood is very ___ and peaceful.
There ___ a small park where children play.
There are many local ___ near my house.

details.title: Social Media and Young People
details.description: Give your opinion on young people spending a lot of time on social media.
sampleStems: Young people today spend a lot of time on social media platforms like Facebook and TikTok. Is this a positive or negative trend? Write at least 80 words.

details.title: A Trip to Our Local Market
details.description: This lesson helps learners understand descriptions of local markets. They will practice identifying types of goods, the atmosphere, and specific details about the market.
details.theorySummary: rule: When reading about a place like a market, look for words that describe what it looks, sounds, and smells like. Pay attention to the types of things sold, the people who are there, and the overall feeling of the place. Adjectives and sensory words are very helpful. | tip: Markets sell many different items. Scan the text for categories of goods (e.g., 'fresh produce,' 'clothes,' 'handicrafts') and specific examples (e.g., 'vegetables,' 'fish,' 'shirts'). This helps you understand the variet…
sampleStems: When do the writer and their mother go to the local market?
What kind of market is it?
What do the farmers sell at the vegetable stalls?

details.description: Learners will read about the common uses of a smartphone in daily life and answer questions about basic technology.
sampleStems: What is the main topic of the passage?
What does the writer use their smartphone for to communicate?
What kind of information can the writer find on their smartphone?

details.title: Talk About Helping Others
details.description: Learn to discuss ways you help others and why it's important to you.
details.theorySummary: rule: When talking about helping others, use a warm and empathetic tone of voice. This can involve slightly softer volume and a gentle, rising-falling intonation pattern to show care and sincerity. | example: Use these phrases: 'I often help [person/group] by [action]...', 'It makes me feel [emotion]...', 'It's important to [verb]...', 'I believe in [value]...', 'I try to [action]...' | tip: Don't just state that you help; give a specific example. For instance, instead of 'I help my family', sa…
sampleStems: Someone who offers their time for free to help others is a ______.
It's important to ______ your friends when they are sad.
Helping others builds a stronger ______.

details.title: Describe a Recent Trip
details.description: Learn to use past tenses and travel vocabulary to describe your holiday experiences.
sampleStems: Where ___ you go on your last summer holiday?
I stayed in a small ___ near the beach for three nights.
We went ___ in the old town to see the famous buildings.

details.title: Describe a Festival
details.description: Learn to describe a festival using the simple present and past tenses. Practice using descriptive adjectives and sequencing events.
details.theorySummary: rule: Use the simple present tense to describe general facts about the festival (e.g., 'It is celebrated in January.'). Use the simple past tense to describe your personal experience at the festival (e.g., 'I went last year.'). | example: Correct: 'The festival is colorful and lively.' or 'We saw beautiful decorations.' (Uses adjectives to make it interesting). Incorrect: 'The festival good.' (Missing 'is'). Adjectives like 'traditional', 'exciting', 'delicious', 'loud', 'bright' are useful. | …
sampleStems: Tet is the most important ___ in Vietnam.
People usually ___ Tet in late January or early February.
Families ___ their houses with flowers and lights.

details.title: Future with 'going to' Grammar
details.description: Practice forming sentences using 'going to' for future plans and predictions.
sampleStems: I am ___ (visit) my aunt next weekend.
She is ___ (study) for her exam tonight.
We are ___ (have) a party on Saturday evening.

details.title: Making a New Friend at School
details.description: This lesson helps learners understand social interactions and the process of making new friends. They will practice identifying key events and understanding reasons for actions.
details.theorySummary: rule: When reading about people meeting, pay attention to who starts the conversation, what they talk about, and what activities they do together. These details show how a relationship develops. Look for dialogue and descriptions of actions. | tip: People do things for reasons. Look for words like 'because,' 'so,' 'to,' or phrases that explain 'why.' For example, if someone 'smiled because she was friendly,' you understand the reason for her action. This helps with inference. | example: Words l…
sampleStems: Who is the new girl in the class?
How did Linh seem at first?
What did An ask Linh to do first?

details.title: A Train Trip to Da Nang
details.description: Learners will read about a family's train journey and answer questions about their travel experience.
sampleStems: What is the main topic of the passage?
How long was the train journey to Da Nang?
What did the family see from the train window?

details.title: Describe a Skill You Are Learning
details.description: Practice talking about a new skill you are acquiring, why you chose it, and your progress.
details.theorySummary: rule: Ensure you pronounce the '-ing' ending clearly, like the 'ng' in 'sing', not like 'ink'. For example, 'learning' should sound like /lɜːrnɪŋ/, not /lɜːrnɪnk/. | example: Use these phrases: 'I'm currently learning to [skill]...', 'It's challenging but fun.', 'I practice by [method]...', 'I decided to learn it because...', 'My goal is to [achieve something]...' | tip: Always explain *why* you are learning a skill or *why* it's important to you. Using 'because' helps you provide clear reasons…
sampleStems: To become very good at a skill, you need to ______ it.
I ______ playing the piano every day to improve.
Learning a new language can be ______ but rewarding.

details.title: A Childhood Memory
details.description: Share a distinct memory from when you were a child.
sampleStems: Talk about a happy childhood memory. How old were you? What happened, and why do you still remember it today? Speak for about 60 seconds.

details.title: A Shopping List and Budget
details.description: Learn to create a simple shopping list and estimate costs. Practice using numbers and expressing needs.
details.theorySummary: rule: When making a shopping list, write down the item and the quantity you need. For example: 'Milk (1 carton)', 'Apples (2 kg)'. Use simple nouns and numbers. | example: Correct: 'I need to buy some bread.' or 'I want to buy new shoes.' (Clearly states what you require). Incorrect: 'Buy bread.' (Too direct for a personal list, sounds like an order). These phrases are polite and clear. | tip: After listing items, try to guess the price of each item. Then, add them up to get a total budget. Use…
sampleStems: I need to ___ some groceries from the market.
On my shopping ___, I have milk, bread, and eggs.
A carton of milk usually ___ about 30,000 VND.

details.description: Discuss the differences between studying at home and studying in a classroom.
sampleStems: Some students prefer studying at home instead of going to school. What are the good and bad points of studying at home? Write at least 80 words.

details.title: Taking the Bus to School
details.description: This lesson helps learners understand how to use public transport. They will practice identifying the sequence of actions and specific details about a journey.
details.theorySummary: rule: When reading about a process, like taking public transport, pay close attention to the order of actions. Look for words like 'first,' 'then,' 'next,' 'after that,' and 'finally.' These words help you follow the steps correctly and understand the journey. | tip: For travel texts, focus on details like the type of transport, the starting point, the destination, how to pay, and any specific instructions. These are often tested in comprehension questions. Scan for names of places, numbers, an…
sampleStems: What kind of public transport does the writer use?
Where does the writer wait for the bus?
What time does the writer usually arrive at the bus stop?

details.description: Learners will read about someone's experience learning a new skill, playing the guitar, and answer questions about the learning process.
sampleStems: What new skill is the writer learning?
When did the writer start guitar lessons?
What is the teacher's name?

details.title: Your Opinion on the Internet

details.description: Develop critical thinking skills by identifying bias and evaluating the credibility of news.
sampleStems: Readers should be wary of ___ headlines that prioritize clicks over accuracy.
The journalist was accused of ___ because of her close ties to the politician.
A reliable news source will always ___ its facts before publishing.
